title: Git still has the work you just deleted
topic: getting deleted commits back with git reflog

alternates: You just wiped three days of commits. Git still has them.
hook.headline: 3 DAYS OF WORK, GONE?

facts.claim: A git commit records a snapshot of the project's staged contents
A branch in Git is a lightweight movable pointer to a commit
git reset --hard discards changes and moves the branch back to an earlier commit
Reflogs record when the tips of branches were updated in the local repository
Reflog entries are kept for 90 days by default before git gc may expire them

beats.narration: Every commit saves a snapshot of your whole project.
beats.headline: 1 COMMIT = 1 SNAPSHOT

beats.narration: Commit often, and the snapshots stack up into nine save points.
beats.headline: 9 SAVE POINTS

beats.narration: Then one hard reset throws the last three away.
beats.headline: RESET --HARD HEAD~3

beats.narration: But git reflog remembers every place your branch has been.
beats.headline: REFLOG LOGS EVERY MOVE

beats.narration: Reset back to that line and your work is home. Git keeps those entries for ninety days.
beats.headline: 90 DAYS TO GET IT BACK

cta.narration: Save this for your next scary reset. Comment GIT for the cheat sheet.
cta.headline_b: SAVE IT FOR YOUR NEXT RESET
